record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: Can one develop effective numerical methods for controllability and optimal control problems for stochastic distributed parameter systems, including numerical solution of the required adjoint equations and forward-backward stochastic evolution equations, beyond the limited existing results?

evidence.quote: (13) Numerics of the controllability and optimal control problems for SDPSs. By generalizing J.-L. Lions’ HUM ..., one can find the numerical solution to controllability problems of SDPSs by solving suitable adjoint equations numerically ... On the other hand, by Theorem 3.4, one can obtain an optimal control by solving suitable forward–backward stochastic evolution equation. Unfortunately, the numerical approximation of the equations mentioned above can be quite cumbersome. ... There are lots of things to be done.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider stochastic distributed parameter systems (SDPSs), i.e., controlled evolution equations of the form

  dy(t) = (A y(t) + B u(t) + f(t,y(t))) dt + (C y(t) + g(t,y(t))) dW(t),  y(0) = y_0,

posed on a separable Hilbert space H, where A generates a C_0-semigroup, B is a bounded control operator, C is a (possibly unbounded) noise coefficient, W is a cylindrical Wiener process on a Hilbert space, and u is an admissible control process adapted to the filtration generated by W. Associated with such systems are two classes of problems:

(i) Exact/approximate/null controllability: characterize and constructively compute, via a Hilbert Uniqueness Method (HUM)-type duality, control processes u steering y(0) = y_0 to a prescribed target at time T > 0; equivalently, solve the associated adjoint backward stochastic evolution equation

  dz(t) = -(A^* z(t) + ...) dt + Z(t) dW(t),  z(T) = z_T,

for the pair (z, Z) of adapted processes.

(ii) Optimal control: minimize a cost functional J(u) = E[∫_0^T ℓ(t,y,u) dt + h(y(T))] subject to the SDPS, where optimal controls are characterized by a coupled forward–backward stochastic evolution equation (FBSEE) on H involving the state y and adjoint pair (z, Z).

Problem. Develop effective, convergent, and computationally implementable numerical methods for:

(a) the adjoint backward stochastic evolution equations arising from HUM-type duality for controllability of SDPSs, together with the construction of approximate HUM controls and quantitative error estimates;

(b) the forward–backward stochastic evolution equations characterizing optimal controls of SDPSs, including space–time discretization schemes (e.g., finite element / spectral in space, time-stepping with conditional expectation approximation) with provable stability and convergence rates in suitable norms.

Specifically, design discretization schemes, prove well-posedness of the discrete problems, establish convergence as the spatial mesh and temporal step tend to zero, and analyze the resulting controllability/optimality gap, going beyond the few presently available results which are limited to special cases (e.g., scalar stochastic heat or wave equations with additive noise, or specific HUM implementations).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open research direction concerning numerical methods for controllability and optimal control of stochastic distributed parameter systems. While there is ongoing work on numerical approximation of backward and forward–backward stochastic (P)DEs and some HUM-based numerical results for stochastic heat/wave equations, no comprehensive theory exists, and the literature explicitly identifies this as an open program with much remaining to be done.
